notes: Fog-of-war regression suite. The DEFAULT pass captures the static grid-reveal scene (fog_zoom2/4/8_origin): a visible reveal circle, an explored memory band, and unexplored black, plus the #2008 column-cull pillar canary — the general FOG_TO_TRIXEL + per-voxel-column-clip guard. The 'edge' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zoom (a static analytic vision circle at the origin with VOXEL objects straddling its boundary) and gates the fog CUT-FACE cross-section (#2125, epic #2124 P1): a boundary-cut voxel object caps with a filled interior wall instead of a see-through hole. The scene also carries a thick ground slab spanning the disc; its cut RIM gates the screen-space cross-section silhouette (#2124 follow-up): the own-column drop keeps the boundary cells the disc crosses (nearest-cell test) so FOG_TO_TRIXEL trims the rim to the analytic disc at game resolution instead of stair-stepping on the voxel lattice. The 'detached' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --detached-edge (the same origin vision circle but the boundary-straddling object is a world-placed DETACHED_REVOXELIZE solid on its own canvas + pool) and gates the detached cross-section (#2127, epic #2124 P3): a detached canvas carries no fog of its own, so this proves the world fog + observers thread into its STAGE_1/2 dispatch and each voxel's world column is recovered from worldCellOffset — it cross-sections like the GRID twin instead of rendering whole. The 'edge_smooth' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-smooth — the SAME geometry as --edge-zoom but a wide soft vision-circle band (Mode B, #2126 P2): the object silhouette + cut wall fade on the smooth disc curve like the floor (the own-column drop keeps partially-revealed columns so FOG_TO_TRIXEL trims them), rather than ending hard at the binary radius. The 'edge_sdf_blocker' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-sdf-blocker — the SAME --edge-zoom voxel scene PLUS one SDF box carrying C_LightBlocker{blocksLOS_=true} straddling the -Y disc arc (#2247): #2247 reported an SDF blocker's fog-hidden half black-banding the cut instead of capping. Master's geometric cut cap (#2274) is content-independent — the box's rendered surface caps at the disc boundary regardless of any occlusion bitfield, so its -Y half fills with the toned cut wall like the -X voxel slab. This is the ENABLED-path gate proving a blocksLOS_ SDF straddling the disc still caps (the cap does not special-case blockers) — a scene WITHOUT the box (the other runs) proves nothing about it. The 'edge_zcost' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost — the vision disc as an XY radius with a Z-COST HEIGHT penalty (#2260): the observer sits at floor level, a central tall voxel pillar at the observer's XY has its base revealed and its top penalized past the disc (dist_xy + zCost*|z - observerZ|) so it fades then drops, and a low cube at the same XY band stays fully revealed. This is the ENABLED-path gate for the height penalty (every other run passes zCost 0, so they prove nothing about it); those other runs are the byte-identity gate that zCost 0 is a no-op. The 'edge_zcost_asym' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost-asym — #2557's generalization to ASYMMETRIC up/down costs: an up pillar (same geometry as edge_zcost's) fades fast under the larger up-cost, and a SEPARATE short down-side block (its own, closer, XY offset — see the kEdgeZCostAsymDownXOffset comment in main.cpp for why it isn't a mirror of the up pillar's reach: the render cull's visible iso viewport is asymmetric in Z at this camera pose) stays mostly revealed under the much smaller down-cost. Positive-fire verified during implementation: forcing zCostDown to mirror zCostUp measurably shrinks/darkens the down block (img_diff ~1.1% drift concentrated in its ROI) versus the shipped asymmetric costs. The 'edge_zcost_ceiling' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost-ceiling — #2557's penalty-free height BAND + near-radius up-cost: the same edge_zcost pillar/cube geometry, but matter within the band reveals fully then cuts off within ~1 unit past it, a hard ceiling instead of a linear fade. Positive-fire verified during implementation: forcing freeBand to 0 nearly drops the pillar and cube entirely (img_diff ~35% drift) versus the shipped band-8 costs, which keep them mostly revealed. The zcost rows also gate the FIELD invariant: stage 1's world drop is z-free, so a height-hidden sample stays in the geometry and FOG_TO_TRIXEL paints it the unexplored colour (black by default) — the pillar keeps its full height and top face instead of a hollow shorter box with the floor behind it. The 'edge_zcost_ceiling_paint' EXTRA RUN re-runs --edge-zcost-ceiling with --fog-debug-color (unexplored colour magenta) so painted-hidden matter reads apart from the black background; the same run logs FOG-PAINT-PROBE (the central pillar's texel count and how many carry the debug colour). Its third shot, fog_edge_zcost_ceiling_paint_yaw9, parks a non-cardinal yaw (0.35 rad) so the scene renders through the per-axis rotation route, which the per-axis fog pass paints at one sample per occupied face. The above-ceiling pillar therefore retains its full height and carries the magenta unexplored colour instead of rendering lit or ending at the ceiling. The 'peraxis_overflow' EXTRA RUN adds a low fog-hidden box large enough to overflow the primary per-axis winner array; its rotated shot and FOG-PERAXIS-PROBE gate both compacted-cell and overflow-entry paint. The 'entity_reveal' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --entity-reveal — fog BODY subjects under the edge_zcost_ceiling band and up-cost: an untagged voxel pillar (adopted as a BODY within one frame) and a governed one render whole above the hard ceiling at one uniform factor (the entity-id fog BODY bit plus its 8-bit factor make FOG_TO_TRIXEL skip the field, the height terms, the rim fade and the cut cap for their pixels), a governed pillar straddling the disc rim renders whole too, a FIELD-tagged control column at the same anchor distance clips per sample (painted above the ceiling, rim fade on its outer columns), a flagged SDF box renders whole while its unflagged twin clips (shapes take the BODY route in a later child), a governed pillar outside every circle stays hidden, and an EXEMPT pillar (marker at construction) outside every circle renders whole. The same run logs FOG-BODY-PROBE per body: the after-fog / before-fog luminance ratio range over the body's texels, the texels above the ceiling, and the texels carrying the cut-face bit. The 'entity_reveal_soft' EXTRA RUN re-runs the same scene with --entity-reveal-soft-edge (edge softness 4): the rim pillar's anchor verdict lands inside the hysteresis band, so the whole body renders at one dimmed factor. Each extra run emits exactly its kEdgeShots/kDetachedEdgeShots/kEdgeSmoothShots/kEdgeSdfBlockerShots/kEdgeZCostShots/kEdgeZCostAsymShots/kEdgeZCostCeilingShots/kEdgeZCostCeilingPaintShots/kPerAxisOverflowShots/kEntityRevealShots/kEntityRevealSoftShots, so capture_offset 0 maps them 1:1. All gated scenes except fog_edge_zcost_ceiling_paint_yaw9 and fog_peraxis_overflow_yaw9 are static + cardinal-yaw-0 with identity-rotation detached solids (the source re-voxelize path — a spinning solid round-to-cell speckles, #1557), verified bit-deterministic run-to-run on macOS (0 drift). The demo's other modes (--moving-observer orbit, --player-walk) are intentionally NOT gated here — they advance a per-frame float center, so they are non-deterministic by construction (manual / attach-screenshots inspection aids). Reference PNGs live in sibling subdirs per CMake preset (macos-debug/, linux-debug/) since Metal and OpenGL produce pixel-different output; linux-debug/ is captured on a Linux/OpenGL host (fleet:needs-linux-smoke) — a backend without committed references SKIPS rather than fails, so bless it there with render-verify --update-references. Shot order mirrors kShots[] / kEdgeShots[] / kDetachedEdgeShots[] / kEdgeSmoothShots[] / kEdgeSdfBlockerShots[] / kEdgeZCostShots[] / kEdgeZCostAsymShots[] / kEdgeZCostCeilingShots[] / kEdgeZCostCeilingPaintShots[] / kPerAxisOverflowShots[] / kEntityRevealShots[] / kEntityRevealSoftShots[] in main.cpp. The 'occlusion*' EXTRA RUNS re-run with --occlusion=<scene> and gate line-of-sight fog (every circle gated, plain disc, straight-down sun) with the exact per-pixel segment march, so every shadow edge is the straight line the occluder's edge projects to: a ground observer reveals the near slab and the ridge's facing wall while the ridge top (the eye is below it) and the slab behind the ridge stay black (occlusion); the same observer standing on the ridge top, the eye 1.5 above it, reveals the far slab past six units from the ridge's far edge, the strip in the ridge's own shadow staying dark (occlusion_high_ground); an SDF box occludes with C_LightBlocker{blocksLOS_=true} (occlusion_blocker) and not with false, where it still renders (occlusion_blocker_inert); two sources offset across a long wall each reveal only their own side (occlusion_two_sources); a gated disc over bare flat ground reveals like an ungated one (occlusion_flat). The 'occlusion_high_ground_soft' EXTRA RUN re-runs the high-ground scene with --los-softness=1: the base strip's far edge fades over one unit of clearance above the ridge top instead of stepping, while the flank stays a crisp line. Each emits one kOcclusion*Shots entry. STRAIGHT-EDGE GATES (structural, render-fog-los-edge-metric.py): the occlusion and occlusion_high_ground passes also fit a line through the 50 % luminance crossing of every scanline of an ROI that crosses exactly one shadow edge and gate the RMS residual — the ground observer's two flank edges (the -Y flank down its columns, the +Y flank along rows below the reveal rim) and, from the ridge top, the base strip's far edge where it emerges past the ridge's -Y corner (the rest of that edge lies under the ridge's own top face on screen). The exact march reads 0.6 / 1.1 / 1.0 px RMS on this host (the trixel lattice's own quantization, 4 x 2 screen px at this pose); the previous cell-quantized gate read 6.1 / 11.4 / 13.4 px, so max_rms 1.5 / max_px 3.0 separate them by a wide margin. ROIs are authored at 2560 x 1440 (roi_at) and scale to a 1x host, where the scanline counts halve — min_scanlines is set below that. The 'world_pan' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --world-pan and gates the camera-anchored fog window over a persisted field: an SDF floor strip from x=-300 to x=3000 with a revealed disc at the origin and one at (2400, 0), painted magenta where unexplored; the four shots jump origin -> far -> origin -> far at zoom 2, each jump a window move and an eviction pass, so the disc left behind is saved and evicted and reloads on return (the FOG-WORLD-PAN probe line per shot carries the window origin, the field statistics since the previous shot, the far disc's resident state and the floor's texel counts). Positive-fire: the fixed 256 window read visible out of window, so the far pose painted nothing magenta; a fixed window under the unexplored contract fogged the whole far floor. The 'depth_slab' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --depth-slab and gates the window's coverage contract: a green 8x8x1 platform inside the camera depth slab (z=-120) near a canvas corner at zoom 1 renders, a red one far outside it (z=-(W/2+64)) under the canvas centre has its columns outside the window and is culled as unexplored; shot 2 parks yaw pi/4 (the per-axis rotation route), where the depth shift is axis-aligned. The FOG-DEPTH-SLAB probe counts each platform's hue in the composited framebuffer. Positive-fire: a tap that reads visible out of window renders the red platform. The 'many_sources' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --many-sources and gates the vision-source tier: sixteen static radius-5 sources on a radius-30 ring over the plain floor with the grid all unexplored, the first eight (0, 45, ... degrees) analytic and smooth, the last eight (22.5 + k x 45 degrees) past the cap and stamped into the world field's transient layer, so they render as cell-quantized discs on floor no analytic disc reaches. The FOG-TIER probe line reads analytic=8 field=8, the visible cell count and each tier centre's cell state (255). Positive-fire: with the tier dropping sources past the cap, those eight discs stay black and fieldCells reads 0. The 'explored_decay' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --explored-decay and gates the explored-state policy and the per-cell channels over a persisted DECAY field: FIELD panels on a floor at the origin (explored memory on the default channel, explored memory shielded on channel 2, a VISIBLE disc) and at (2400, 0) (explored memory), plus two source panels under the eighth (analytic) and ninth (field-tier) channel-2 sources, each split into a channel-2 half and a default half, and a fog-hidden box outside the eighth disc's rim. The creation's clock is 0 for shot 1 and one duration for the rest, so shot 1 shows the memory explored, shot 2 the same pose with the default-channel memory painted magenta while the shielded memory and the VISIBLE disc stand, shot 3 the far panel expired after the window moved, shot 4 the return with nothing resurrected, and shot 5 a non-cardinal yaw (0.35 rad, the per-axis routes and the overflow lane) over the source panels. On every route the channel-2 halves reveal and the default halves stay painted whole. The FOG-EXPLORED-DECAY probe line per shot carries the clock, the expired-cell count, each panel's painted/total texels and the exact uploaded (state, mask) texels at the memory and shielded centres; it exits non-zero on any violation. Positive-fire: disabling expiry leaves shot 2's memory panel unpainted; dropping the cell-mask intersection reveals the default halves. The 'ceiling' and 'ceiling_treatment' EXTRA RUNS re-run with --ceiling-treatment (plus --reveal-treatment for the second): one soft disc (radius 14, edge 2) from an observer on the slab's top plane, capped by a soft ceiling 5 above it fading over 4, over a centre and a rim FIELD column of equal height (4x4x16) and a governed BODY twin anchored under the ceiling, unexplored matter painted magenta; the cardinal shot (fog_ceiling9 / fog_ceiling_treatment9) runs FOG-SURFACE-PROBE, which grades each column's first-hidden and fully-hidden voxel level on the GPU against the CPU oracle (hash-aware under the treatment), requires the centre and rim to cut at the same levels, the silhouette above the band to be painted whole, and under the treatment a nonzero dissolved, retained and cap-toned count (zero on the control), while the BODY twin must rise above the ceiling whole and uniform; the yaw shots (fog_ceiling_yaw9 / fog_ceiling_treatment_yaw9) park 0.35 rad so the same columns render through the per-axis routes. The 'occlusion_high_ground_soft_treated' EXTRA RUN is the high-ground soft row with --reveal-treatment: the same FOG-SURFACE-PROBE over the slab reports the soft line-of-sight band's dissolved, retained and cap-toned texels, zero disagreements with the oracle's hash decision, and a band under a tenth of the slab; the untreated row is unchanged. Positive-fire: with the treatment off every band voxel is retained and none is toned.
